chapter: Jazz at the Philharmonic and life on the road
title: Gambling on cards: Los Angeles games and JATP travel
summary: When she arrived in Los Angeles people played blackjack, poker and pinochle for hundreds of dollars for days. On JATP tours she, Flip Phillips and Roy Eldridge played cards on trains and planes, and she enjoyed travelling with men.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Isn't that something? How about that. And do you play any cards these days?
No, I don't play cards anymore. I used to play cards.
Did you ever play pinuckle?
Yeah, because when I first came out here that's all they used to do.
Was it?
Yeah, play cards. They used to play black jack, poker, pinuckle.
And bet a little bit.
Oh yeah.
What did people bet? What kind of stakes?
Any kind of stakes. You'd think everybody was a millionaire.
Oh my.
The way they was betting. Two, three, four, five hundred dollars, you know.
Oh, really?
Yeah.

Did the games go on for four or five hours?
Four or five hours? Four or five days. It could go on for days.
Oh wow.
And then go to work and come home get a fast bath and and/run on over to the game and sit there all night, the rest of the night and day; run home and get in the bath and get ready to go to work.
Oh Helen.
Oh, used to do that around the clock.
You mean you'd work without having had any sleep?
Yes.
(Walker)
Well you know T-Bone used to tell me all about this but I didn't. . .
Yeah, that's what we used to do.
Do you remember you did the Blues Festival in 1962 and T-Bone was on that.
Yeah.
Did he play some cards then? Were you playing any cards then or were you traveling too
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
No, we was traveling then.
Yeah.

But like when we would get on the plane or something, we'd sit there and play a little cards. I remember when I was with Jazz at the Philharmonic. Well honey, Flip Phillips and Roy and all of us, we were playing cards all over and then we'd get on the train, you know; well whoever would get on first would go and get the seats and get the table so we could all get together. And we just played cards all over the United States.
How funny. There's a way you can tell something about a guy by the way he plays, isn't there? I mean, not all guys can take to losing, can they?
No, but you know, they'd all try and be slick but you can read them.
Tell me about it?
I don't know, they just started to do alot of talking . . .
And distract you?

And make you think different?
Yeah, but you just pay them no attention, and you got them. It was fun, I'll tell you. I like traveling with a bunch of fellows.
Well you were usually the only gal.
Yes.
So that makes you kind of special.
Yes.
